pattern.crimePattern: a young pharmacist selling counterfeit medicines under forged supplier invoices poisons the inspector who found them, with a drugged soda
pattern.notes: Fictional pharmacy, distributor and inspectors. The sedative is never named and no dose is given. The forgery's flaw (batch numbers that do not exist) is shown, never how invoices are faked.

ob.text: A woman is reported dead in her parked car on Meru's main street, 50 metres from a pharmacy. Kanini Wambua (44), Pharmacy and Poisons Board inspector. Suspected heart attack.

facts.text: Kanini Wambua, PPB inspector, was found dead in her parked car on Meru's main street, 50 metres from Tumaini Chemists.
She was slumped over the wheel; an empty soda bottle in the cup holder; no inspection notice in her bag.
The engine was off and the windows were down.
A hawker told the first officer she "collapsed at sunset, about half six".
Kanini's carbon book: a notice at 17:20 to Tumaini Chemists, six products not on the manufacturer's register, premises to close 09:00 Friday, invoices to be seized. The top copy is torn out.
Kanini's tablet: photos at 17:05 of six packs on Tumaini's shelf; the register says "batch not found" for all six.
Two control packs from the same shelf come back "found".
ATM camera: Kanini enters Tumaini at 16:58 and leaves at 17:25 holding a soda bottle.
ATM camera: her car parked in a marked bay; no warden, no argument.
Tumaini: six gaps on the shelf; the same batches in the stockroom in boxes of 200.
Supplier invoices from "Kirinyaga Pharma Distributors" list those batch numbers.
The soda crate counted that morning: "24". Now 23.
Controlled-drugs register, Thursday 17:10: 20 tablets of a strong sedative "for patient", no prescription number, initials B.J.
PPB licence: owner S. Muthaura; pharmacist in charge B. Jepkemboi, with her specimen signature.
Kirinyaga Pharma: "We don't stock those brands. That PIN on the invoice is ours, but the invoice number series ended in 2023."
A genuine Kirinyaga Pharma invoice: the current number series, laser-printed, the KRA PIN.
Grace: Kanini suspended Abdikadir Ali's company's licence last year. Grace was at the PPB office until 17:30 (the sign-out book).
Records, Brenda's line: Thursday 17:40, a 6-minute call to a number registered at the Meru bus park.
In Brenda's stove ash pan: the torn-out inspection notice, half burned.
In her drawer: blank invoice paper with the distributor's logo.
Silas was in Nairobi all week, at his hotel and meetings.
His company's Nyeri office: Abdikadir at a sales meeting 14:00–19:00.
Mark gives his fingerprints voluntarily.
Fingerprints taken from Brenda in detention.
Autopsy: no heart disease. Death by respiratory depression.
Toxicology: a heavy dose of the sedative in her blood and in the soda bottle. Death between 17:30 and 18:00.
Lab: Kanini's and Brenda's prints on the bottle. Not Mark's.
Comparison view: the batch numbers on the invoices are not on the manufacturer's register, and their invoice series ended years ago.
The invoices carry no stamp: a printed logo and a PIN.
A supplier invoice has no witnesses, no exam index number and no parcel number.
The receiving signature on the invoices matches Brenda's specimen signature on the licence: her own.
Wilfrida Ayugi: forged. Inkjet-printed; the logo copied from the distributor's website.

reconstruction.text: Brenda buys cheap counterfeit antimalarials and antibiotics from a man at the bus park and covers them with invoices printed in the name of a real distributor, with invented batch numbers. The profit is hers; the owner never looks.

Thursday, 16:58. Kanini walks in, photographs six packs at 17:05, and gets "batch not found" six times. Two control packs come back "found". She tells Brenda quietly she'll close her at nine tomorrow and take the invoices.
17:10. Brenda signs out 20 sedative tablets from the cabinet, "for patient", and takes a cold soda into the back room while Kanini writes her notice.

17:25. Kanini leaves holding the soda. She drives 50 metres, parks to make a call, and slumps over the wheel. Brenda takes the top copy of the notice from the passenger seat while people are still gathering.
17:40. Brenda calls the bus park. That night she burns the notice in her stove.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Brenda and a warrant on her flat. Detain her after the search; toxicology takes 18 h, still inside her 24, with the prints (6 h) and the invoice examination (10 h) running alongside.

ui.beatNotes: Batch lookup. The player types a batch number into Kanini's tablet; it answers "found" or "not found". Genuine packs from the same shelf come back "found", teaching the player to check a control sample before trusting a "not found". The bus-park counterfeiter goes to the Pattern File as a lead (not a spine thread).
